files.basis: New file provenance tooling authored for the 2026-09-27 migration goal; uses Node built-ins and Git metadata, no copied upstream implementation. The 2026-09-28 extension adds digest-bound, non-authorizing retained-nature reviews, accepted-only overlapping statistics and one evidenced host-manifest alias; it preserves upstream and third-party facts and existing conflict/expiry rules. New requirements were tested before implementation. The 2026-09-30 reconciliation adds specifically evidenced path aliases, digest-bound unresolved asset evidence and shared third-party audit entry checks; existing source origins, retained-nature reviews, file-local notices and licence boundaries are preserved. Regression requirements preceded these changes.

Independently authored offline publisher-source audit; checks a pinned Git commit and retained license before comparing SVG byte digests. No source assets are copied or transformed. Regression requirements preceded these changes. Historical Material Icon Theme references are byte-reproduced and individually bound to declared commit/scope/blob/license; unverified assets and all original provenance remain retained.

The dispatch design uses one explicit FIFO owner per normalized session, a separate promise-only completion registry and shared close barrier, and a stdio instance owner. Eighteen public behavior groups ran against the prior server: eleven passed and seven exposed unscoped-key collision, premature or incomplete closure, late success, and skipped cleanup. The independent scheduling/lifecycle composition passes those groups and four stdio ownership/reentrant-construction groups plus two structured error cancellation groups. Review found and reproduced a constructor-close leak and loss of explicit/fallback isError diagnostics in the initial design; tests failed before the targeted corrections and now pass. Actual built MCP checks serial/concurrent routing and closed discovery, while the unchanged stable executable URL still starts real isolated workers. Argument fields, schema constraints, exported names, environment names, protocol text and external SDK calls are retained interoperability requirements; those facts alone do not prove originality. Source access is disclosed and this is not a no-access clean-room claim. Third-party MCP/Zod and the remaining plugin loader, core, desktop and UI are outside this limited license decision.
